prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1329; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver side rear quarter panel. Claimant reports neck pain and a headache and states she was evaluated at an urgent care facility and told she may have a concussion. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Liability questions to be reviewed once the scene report is received.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. She confirms she was in the adjacent lane when the insured vehicle drifted into her path. Insured driver states he checked his mirror but did not see the claimant's vehicle in his blind spot. Claimant says she has not yet seen a physician for follow-up and is experiencing dizziness, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating at work. Advised claimant on medical documentation needs and the process for submitting bills and records.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report. The responding officer noted both vehicles had visible damage consistent with a sideswipe and cited the insured driver for failure to maintain lane. Two independent witnesses are listed in the report. Requested the dashcam footage from the insured and a copy of the claimant's urgent care records, which she has agreed to provide. Preliminary liability assessment leans toward the insured.

Entry 4: Claimant has retained no attorney as of this entry, but she asked how the bodily injury portion of the claim is evaluated and whether she should keep a symptom journal. Explained that the claim can be reviewed as a whole and that she may consult an attorney at any time. Provided a list of documents to gather, including neurology or primary care notes, prescriptions, and records of missed work. Scheduled a follow-up call once the records arrive.

Entry 5: Received the urgent care records and the witness statements. Witness two confirms the insured vehicle moved into the claimant's lane without signaling. Dashcam footage from the insured vehicle is under review and appears to show the lane change without a clear view of the claimant's vehicle. Referred the bodily injury component to the medical review unit for evaluation of the concussion diagnosis and recommended a neurological follow-up. Will update the claimant once the review is complete.
